items.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: And he said that Miles used to say he liked music that doesn’t sound like music.

ctx.x: It does. It’s wonderful to hear. It’s really innovative I think. I know what you mean like, you know, you get used to putting your shout chorus three quarters of the way through and, what’s going to happen at the solo, put a background after the solo.

Or that there even is a shout chorus, you know? It’s like what is a shout chorus and why? Hasn’t there been music written for centuries and in different cultures and nobody had a shout chorus. Why in jazz do we always have to have a God damn shout chorus? That’s kind of how I feel. Sometimes I hear large ensemble jazz music, so you know if you think about music, just — like I went to Brazil, you know that probably ‘cause I talked about that hang gliding piece. But I went to Brazil and one of the powerful things…
How do you impart that — some of your philosophies — to other students? Is it possible to do that?
